newsitem.title: FRANCE: Aerospatiale seeks Thomson-CSF, telecoms link.
newsitem.headline: Aerospatiale seeks Thomson-CSF, telecoms link.

text.p: State-owned Aerospatiale seeks closer ties with defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF to strengthen its missiles division, and is looking for a telecommunications partner for its space business.

"For Aerospatiale, it is very important to have an alliance with Thomson in the missiles sector because of everything we do on the surface-to-air missiles Aster and Roland," Aerospatiale chairman Yves Michot recently told journalists.
He also named Alcatel Alsthom and Lockheed Martin as potential telecommunications partners for Aerospatiale's satellite activities.

The previous conservative government ruled out Aerospatiale from bidding for Thomson-CSF in the sale of the state's 58 percent stake but Aerospatiale is watching the situation closely as the two compnaies have a range of common interests.
Thomson-CSF, Aerospatiale and Alenia of Finmeccanica are partners in the Eurosam venture which makes Aster.
Michot said he was waiting for the Socialist government's decision on whether the Thomson-CSF privatisation would go ahead.

It was important that relations between the two French firms are strengthened otherwise there could be a "war" between the electronics and aeronautics poles if Thomson-CSF fell into hostile hands, an Aerospatiale executive said.
Conglomerate Lagardere and telecommunications and engineering group Alcatel Alsthom are rival bidders in the Thomson-CSF sell-off. Lagardere competes directly with Aerospatiale in missiles and space.
Aerospatiale is looking for a telecommunications alliance following agreements signed between Lagardere and Daimler-Benz Aerospace (Dasa) in space and missiles, Michot said.

"Taking into account the agreement signed between Dasa and Matra, I do not see the point of Aerospatiale entering the alliance as a junior partner...I would rather have an alliance with a large telecommunications company," he said.
Matra High Technology is a unit of Lagardere.
"Dasa is no longer our privileged partner," Michot added.
Alcatel and Lockheed Martin were among telecommunications groups he listed when asked what companies he had in mind.

The telecommunications sector offers high growth prospects in the satellite business and there was scope for synergy in designing the telecommunications networks and building the satellites, an Aerospatiale executive said.
